# Pi Event Integrity — llms.txt
# A read-only coverage audit and event-integrity engine for Soroban events on Pi
# Network, with a replayable sha256 digest. No network needed for offline modes.

> A walker that reports "N events found" is usually reporting a LOWER BOUND.
> The RPC caps a response at 100 events and does not honour its cursor, so a
> full page cannot be continued. This tool classifies every window, labels the
> total EXACT or LOWER BOUND, lists the unverifiable regions, and carries a
> tamper-evident content digest. It also tracks event identity: duplicate
> detection, gap detection, resume, and independent-source comparison.

## What it is
- read-only, zero-dependency, Node (ESM)
- pure engine: lib.mjs, windows.mjs, audit.mjs, render.mjs
- CLI: audit-cli.mjs

## Four window states
- verified   queried, returned FEWER than the cap  -> provable, exact for the range
- truncated  queried, returned EXACTLY the cap    -> lower bound, NOT provable
- errored    RPC error                            -> nothing known
- skipped    never queried (retention / dry-run)  -> nothing known

## Central rule
- A total is EXACT only when EVERY window is provable.
- Otherwise it is a LOWER BOUND and the unverifiable regions are listed.

## Event identity (measured 2026-10-19)
- every event carries `id` = "{TOID}-{index}", a global ordering key
- TOID is monotonic non-decreasing across a page; ids are distinct within a page
- overlapping windows return DISJOINT pages (0 shared ids), so a repeated id is an anomaly
- an empty ledger inside a verified window is legitimate, not an error
- duplicates: none | exact | UNOBSERVABLE (a truncated window hides a duplicate)
- gaps: empty (provable, verified window) | unproven (NOT reported as a gap)
- resume: continue at the ledger after the last covered window; retention can expire it
- source comparison: agree | disagree | not-comparable (version-scoped, verified-only)

## Digest
- sha256 over a fully specified canonical byte string (docs/DIGEST-SPEC.md)
- one line per window: {start}-{end}|{state}|{eventCountOrNull}|{getEvents}|{startLedger}|{endLedgerExclusive}|{limit}
- UTF-8, lines joined by LF, no trailing newline
- always read with a header: endpoint + node version + protocol version
- verdicts: match | mismatch | not-comparable
- a mismatch means THE RECORD CHANGED, not that any value is wrong
- the identity layer is NOT part of the digest: the two are verified independently

## Usage
- node audit-cli.mjs --from <l> --to <l> [--step 9000] [--json]
- node audit-cli.mjs --from <l> --to <l> --dry-run [--json]
- node audit-cli.mjs --verify <manifest.json>     (offline)
- node audit-cli.mjs --compare <a.json> <b.json>  (offline)
- node audit-cli.mjs --boundaries | --help
- exit 0 all provable | 1 any unprovable | 2 invalid/outside retention
- --compare exit 0 agree | 1 disagree | 2 not-comparable

## Measured (2026-10-19, rpc.testnet.minepi.com, node 28.0.1, protocol 28)
- events per response: at most 100; `limit` is ignored
- `cursor` returned but not honoured: a full page cannot be continued
- endLedger is EXCLUSIVE ([L,L] -> 0 events)
- retention: 120960 ledgers (~7 days at 5 s/ledger)
- a 120960-ledger walk in 14 windows: 100% ledger coverage, 14/14 truncated,
  events_found >= 1400 (LOWER BOUND), exit 1, duplicates UNOBSERVABLE
- a single recent ledger: verified, EXACT, exit 0
- a verified 20-ledger window: 83 events, 83 distinct ids, ordered,
  duplicates none (provable), 3 empty ledgers (legitimate), exit 0
- Mainnet Soroban RPC: not reachable (HTTP 503)

## Not claimed
- that an event set is complete
- that events_found is a total when any window is unprovable
- that no duplicate exists (only whether one was observed)
- that a ledger inside an unproven window is empty
- that a resume always works (retention can expire the resume point)
- that a truncated window agrees or disagrees with anything
- that a digest proves the RPC is unchanged
- that a digest is a signature (it is content-addressed, not identity-attested)
- that the 100-event cap is a protocol constant (it is observed and re-measured)
- anything about Mainnet
- that Pi Network has adopted, reviewed, or endorsed this
